site.title: The Week After Christmas
site.subtitle: Five places that work for all ten of us. Sunday December 27, 2026 to Sunday January 3, 2027.
site.disclaimer: Preliminary. Nothing is booked, quoted or decided. Every price is an estimate for ten people at holiday-week rates unless it says published. Flight days are as the airlines announced them and still need to be checked for these dates.
site.party: Mom, Patrick and Sara, Andrew and Trisha, Kristina and Michael with Bennett (7) and Taylor (3), and Daniel. Seven fly from Norfolk, two from Richmond, one from Austin.
rules: One roof, a bedroom for each couple, Mom, Daniel and the kids: six doors, or five plus a real bunk room.
A base you can walk out of: a safe town with things to do on foot, and cars for the group. No compound.
Mom's rule: a nice place to stay and walking options, one anchor a day, split up for specific things and reconvene for dinner.

Food: Sara is strictly gluten-free, no cross-contact, and eats real butter, dairy, eggs and meat. Kristina has a tree-nut allergy. Mom is pescatarian. Every option runs on a house kitchen plus one or two chef nights.
The adventure crew (Patrick, Daniel, Andrew, Mom, Kristina) and the relaxed crew (Sara, Trisha, Michael, the kids) each get a real week, in parallel, from the same house.

trips.name: Puerto Rico
trips.place: Rincón, with Old San Juan at each end
trips.pitch: A pool house in Rincón, a surf town you walk around, with a night in Old San Juan on the way in and the way out so nobody drives the west side in the dark with Taylor. No passports, nonstops from Norfolk and Richmond, US medicine, sea level, real winter surf and a boat dive for the crew, pool and the calm side of the beach for the kids.
why: US soil: no passports, US hospitals and pharmacies, dollars, phones that just work.
JetBlue announced a Sunday nonstop from Norfolk and a Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday nonstop from Richmond. Daniel connects once from Austin.
Real adventure from the door: December surf at Maria's, Domes and Sandy Beach, a two-tank boat dive at Desecheo Island, the Gozalandia waterfall, an Isabela surf day.
Old San Juan on foot at each end: El Morro, the walls, a good dinner.
The cheapest warm option on the list.
catch: December is big-wave season, so the kids stay on the pool and the calm-side beaches, and reef snorkeling is a summer thing.
Gluten-free restaurants are thin. Most meals are at the house, with a chef for two nights.
The best six-bedroom house found is about a mile from the plaza. The one that is an easy walk to town has five bedrooms.
The Norfolk nonstop does not fly Saturdays, and its clock times still need to be confirmed on jetblue.com.
Rincón has no hospital. The nearest ER, with a separate one for kids, is in Aguadilla, about 25 to 30 minutes away by an estimate we still need to drive-check.
trips.weather: Dry-season tropics: highs in the mid-80s, lows around 70, brief trade-wind showers, sea about 80 degrees. Winter swell on the west coast.

getting_there.how: JetBlue nonstop to San Juan, announced for Mon, Wed, Fri and Sun (flight 929 out, 928 back). Sunday Dec 27 out and Sunday Jan 3 back fit the pattern; Mon Dec 28 and Mon Jan 4 are the fallbacks. About 3.5 hours in the air.

JetBlue nonstop Tue, Thu and Sat only, so Andrew and Trisha drive to Norfolk and fly with the group, or fly Sat Dec 26 and Sat Jan 2 with an extra San Juan night, or connect once via Charlotte or Atlanta on the Sundays.
One stop via Charlotte, Dallas, Atlanta or Houston. Southwest's seasonal Austin to San Juan nonstop is unconfirmed for the holiday window.
Two seven-seat vehicles for the week. San Juan to Rincón is about 2.5 hours, done in daylight both ways.

houses.name: Casa Cooky, Corcega side

trips.name: Anna Maria Island
trips.tag: Easiest for the spouses and kids
trips.pitch: A pool house a short walk from the Gulf on a bike-everywhere island with walkable villages. The easiest flights on the list and the best week for the spouses and the kids. The crew gets a manatee morning, a boat day and bikes, not surf or snow.
why: About six hours door to door: Breeze flies Norfolk to Tampa nonstop, Richmond has had the same, and Austin has nonstops to Tampa.
Beach and pool every day for a three-year-old, bikes for a seven-year-old, Pine Avenue and Bridge Street for the adults.
Sarasota and St. Petersburg are 30 to 60 minutes away: the Ringling, Selby Gardens' holiday lights (2026 dates to confirm), the Chihuly Collection (Mom's July trip, continued), the Mote aquarium.
Crystal River manatee snorkel in peak season, about 2 to 2.5 hours up the coast, a boat day to Egmont Key, mangrove paddles.
catch: The thinnest week for the adventure crew. The Gulf is usually flat in December.
Gulf water runs mid to upper sixties, so the pool carries the swimming.
The flagship listing has five true bedrooms plus a den with a bunk and trundle; confirm a real sixth room.
Holiday-week availability on the island is the real question this late. Listed peak rates for six-bedroom houses run $1,755 to $2,251 a night before taxes and fees (checked Oct 21).
One celiac-aware restaurant on the island (The Waterfront, a single undated review). Most meals at the house, with a chef for New Year's Eve.
trips.weather: Highs around 70 to 75, lows in the 50s, Gulf water in the high 60s. Beach and pool weather most days; a cold front can bring wind.

getting_there.how: Breeze Airways nonstop to Tampa, about 2 hours 15 minutes, then about 1 hour 15 minutes by car to Holmes Beach. Frontier is seasonal.
Breeze nonstop to Tampa on last year's schedule, or Sarasota via Breeze; confirm the December days.
Southwest nonstop to Tampa, about 3 daily on weekdays; Delta to Tampa and an Allegiant option to Sarasota (30 minutes from the island) to check.
Two SUVs for the week, plus bikes on the island.

trips.name: Park City
trips.pitch: An Old Town house with Main Street and the Town Lift at the door. The best riding week by a mile and the best town to walk out into. It costs three things: a third winter trip in two years, 7,000 feet of altitude, and a cold week for Michael, Trisha and the kids.
why: Park City Mountain from the Town Lift, a walk from the house, five or six riding days. Canyons Village on the same pass. A Big Cottonwood powder day for the crew.
Main Street: shops, galleries, restaurants, the free trolley, a hot tub at the house every night.
Utah Olympic Park and the Comet bobsled for Kristina, who has wanted to bobsled since Lake Placid (season dates to confirm).
The Viking Yurt sleigh-ride dinner for Mom: the music-with-dinner evening she writes up.
A nonstop for Daniel from Austin to Salt Lake.
catch: A third winter trip in two years, against Mom's own note that not everyone snowboards.
Altitude: Old Town sits near 7,000 feet.
A cold week for the relaxed crew, with highs in the 20s and 30s.
Peak-week pricing: a six-bedroom Old Town house over New Year's runs $35,000 to $55,000 for the week, before flights and lift tickets.
Luna's Kitchen is the one dedicated gluten-free kitchen found in town, counter-service and closed Sundays; the two-kitchen house gives Sara her own kitchen.
trips.weather: Cold, dry, sunny days: highs in the 20s and 30s, lows in the teens. Snow depends on the year; December averages 30 to 65 inches depending on the source.

getting_there.how: One stop to Salt Lake City on Delta via Atlanta, or United via Denver or Washington. A nonstop may exist some days; check Dec 27 and Jan 3. Then 40 minutes to Old Town.

trips.name: Lake Placid
trips.place: The Olympic village, upstate New York
trips.tag: The known quantity, as a fallback
trips.pitch: The family's own February base, done again with the two things that were missing: a house with a hot tub and the kids along. Main Street, the Mirror Lake loop, the Olympic Center and the skating oval are all on foot, Whiteface is twenty minutes by car, and everyone including Mom skied it last time. Two things hold it to a fallback as of October 21: the bobsled ride is listed as unavailable for track updates, and the walkable six-bedroom houses with hot tubs already show booked for the week.
why: The village passes the walk-out test easily: Main Street shops and restaurants, the paved 2.7-mile Mirror Lake loop, outdoor skating on the Olympic oval, dog-sled rides on Mirror Lake daily from December 26, the Olympic Museum and the 1980 arena.
Whiteface, the mountain all five riders skied in February, with snowmaking on nearly every acre; cross-country on the 1932 and 1980 Nordic trails at Mt Van Hoevenberg for Mom at the 70-and-up rate.
A drive, not a flight day: about 10 hours 40 minutes from Virginia Beach with an overnight in the Hudson Valley on the way up, the way Patrick did it last time. Daniel flies to Albany.
The Mirror Lake Inn spa and a reformer studio on Main Street for Sara, the Wild Center and the skating oval for the kids (Taylor skates free), a hot tub for Mom.
About $28,000 to $36,000 for ten with the one house confirmed open, which overlaps Asheville and sits under Puerto Rico.
catch: The bobsled, Kristina's stated reason to come back, is not bookable: the venue's page redirects and the tourism site says it is unavailable for track updates. The skeleton ride that is offered is ages 13 and up, so only the adults could slide.

The walkable six-bedroom houses with hot tubs (Hillcrest Haven, the Stevens house, the Waterfront house) all show booked for December 27 to January 3. The one house confirmed open, Cliff View Loj, is under a mile out, which one reviewer called a 30-minute walk. Camp Kobl Hill, which would decide it, needs a call.
A third winter trip in two years, and the coldest week on the list: highs near 28 degrees, nights near zero.
Ten to eleven hours of driving each way, with winter on I-87 and Route 73 able to add hours.
No dedicated gluten-free restaurant in town; a list of celiac-literate kitchens and the house carry Sara's week. The toboggan chute needs a foot of lake ice, unlikely before January.
trips.weather: Reliably wintry and short-day: December highs about 28 degrees, nights near zero, about 104 inches of snow a year. Whiteface runs on snowmaking across nearly all of its skiable acres.

notes.title: Vermont and Canada, compared
paragraphs: Stowe, Vermont wins on the things Lake Placid lacked last time: a house with a hot tub, a real spa at Topnotch or the Trapp Family Lodge, an Epic mountain for all five riders, and the groomed recreation path from the village. It loses on the drive (12 to 13 hours from Virginia Beach, one to two more than Lake Placid), on the walk-out test unless the house is in the small village, on gluten-free depth and a reformer, and it has no bobsled. Roughly $26,000 to $42,000 for ten, with two six-bedroom hot-tub houses found and neither priced for the week.

Mont-Tremblant, Quebec is the best village of the three: a car-free resort at the lift base, a low mountain (about 750 to 2,900 feet, so altitude is no issue), six-bedroom hot-tub homes a few minutes' walk from the village, the Scandinave spa, dog sledding, tubing and an indoor water park for the kids. It loses on access, which is the thing Mom flags: a one-connection flight to Montreal for all ten plus a 90-minute winter drive and a border crossing, passports for everyone including the kids, Canadian dollars, and cold to 5 below. Roughly $30,000 to $50,000 for ten.

Quebec City scored low in the first round (the old city is a day trip from any ski chalet), and Banff fails on altitude and the Calgary transfer. If the family wants snow more than ease, Tremblant is the one to build out; if it wants the known quantity and a drive, Lake Placid is, once two phone calls settle the bobsled and the house.

getting_there.how: Drive: 10 hours 41 minutes without stops by Google Maps, the family's 11 hours in February. Two cars, an overnight in the Hudson Valley on Saturday December 26, check-in Sunday. Flying is one stop to Albany (American via Philadelphia, United via Washington, Southwest via Baltimore) then about 2.5 hours north.
